Citi maintains "Buy" ratings on TONGCHENGTRAVEL and TRIP.COM-S, with a target price of HK$22 for TONGCHENGTRAVEL and a target price of US$61 for TRIP.COM's US-listed shares. Citi released a research report maintaining "Buy" ratings on TONGCHENGTRAVEL (00780) and TRIP.COM-S (09961), with a target price of HK$22 for Tongcheng and US$61 for Trip.com Group Ltd. Sponsored ADR (TCOM.US). Although the Ministry of Culture and Tourism has not yet released tourism data for the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, the bank expects long-haul travel to perform steadily during the holiday, with the two-year compound growth rate of national passenger volume projected at 1.1%, of which aviation, railway, road, and waterway are expected to grow 9.4%, grow 12.4%, remain flat, and grow 20.7%, respectively; inbound and outbound data show that cross-border passenger volume increased 16.8% year-on-year during the period. As this year's Mid-Autumn Festival is relatively close to the National Day holiday, Citi believes many people will use annual leave to "bridge" and extend their holidays, so the strong performance in aviation and railway passenger volume is not surprising. The bank noted that some travel demand may have been brought forward to the Mid-Autumn Festival, potentially affecting National Day data, but it expects combined demand across the two holidays to still perform ideally year-on-year, indicating that even amid a soft macroeconomic environment, travel demand remains resilient, which it believes will benefit the upcoming results of online travel agencies (OTAs).

Overall, bookings in these cities increased nearly 150%, with spending up nearly 200%. We are also seeing a shift in where and how people travel. Less traditional lower-density destinations are growing faster than major tourist attractions. Short-haul trips, city breaks, rural leisure and educational experiences are becoming increasingly popular. Travelers are also moving beyond single attraction sightseeing toward more immersive experiences that combine tourism with dining, accommodation, transportation, culture and other local offerings. These trends are broadening the addressable opportunity for our platform and creating more ways for travelers to discover and engage with local destinations and businesses. Concerts, sporting events and other live experiences have defined dates and strong fan appeal, making them powerful catalysts for cross-city travel and local consumption. As part of our rectification measures, we are discontinuing our Tier 1 distribution program and transitioning partners to a new multitiered framework, giving them more choices in how they work with us and creating opportunities for shared growth. For the second quarter of 2026, Trip.com Group reported total net revenues of RMB 15.7 billion, representing a 6% increase from the same period last year. This was primarily driven by resilient global travel demand during the quarter. Accommodation reservation revenue for the second quarter was RMB 6.6 billion, representing a 6% increase year-over-year. This was mainly driven by solid growth in international hotel bookings, partially offset by the impact of a contra revenue item related to the administrative penalty imposed by the State Administration for Market Regulation. Excluding this item, revenue would have increased by 8%. Transportation ticketing revenue for the quarter was RMB 5.4 billion, representing a 1% decrease year-over-year. The decline was primarily driven by softer demand across markets, elevated fuel prices and geopolitical tensions as well as operations adjustments related to industry standards and compliance. These factors were partially offset by strong performance from our international OTA platform. Packaged tour revenue for the second quarter was RMB 1.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. This was mainly supported by strong growth on our international OTA platform and continued momentum in customized tours across markets as travelers increasingly sought more personalized experience. Corporate travel revenue for the second quarter was RMB 771 million, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. This reflected continued penetration of our managed corporate travel services among corporate clients. Excluding share-based compensation charges, adjusted product development expenses for the second quarter increased by 7% year-over-year. Adjusted G&A expenses, also excluding the one-off anti-monopoly penalty imposed by the SAMR, increased by 8% year-over-year. The increases were primarily driven by higher personnel-related expenses. Adjusted sales and marketing expenses for the second quarter increased by 15% year-over-year. The increase was mainly driven by heightened marketing efforts in support of our global business expansion. Excluding share-based compensation charges and the antimonopoly penalty imposed by the SAMR, adjusted EBITDA was RMB 4.6 billion for the second quarter compared with RMB 4.9 billion in the same period last year. Excluding share-based compensation charges, the anti-monopoly penalties imposed by the SAMR, fair value changes of equity securities investments and exchangeable senior notes recorded in other income and their tax effects, non-GAAP diluted earnings per ordinary share and per ADS were RMB 7.27 or USD 1.07 for the second quarter of 2026, compared with RMB 7.0 for the same period in 2025. As of June 30, 2026, the balance of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments, held-to-maturity time deposits and financial products was RMB 100.5 billion or USD 14.8 billion. web.title: Expedia Bets Against the All-Powerful AI Travel Agent
web.description: # Expedia Bets Against the All-Powerful AI Travel Agent ... September 23rd, 2026 at 4:17 PM EDT ... Expedia wants a seat inside the new wave of AI agents, including Meta's Muse. But CEO Ariane Gorin is betting on a messier future for travel: multiple entry points and specialized agents, not one bot that owns the whole trip. Speaking at the Skift Global Forum on Wednesday, Expedia CEO Ariane Gorin said she wants to work with  the newest generation of AI agents — including Meta's Muse — but doesn't think any single one can take over the entire travel journey. The company had just revealed on Tuesday that it would be available on Muse, Meta's new AI agent. Its X.com post didn’t detail how that would work, only that it’s “joining @Muse: tell it where you're headed and it can work with Expedia to sort your hotels, and everything in between.” Gorin, participating via remote video, didn’t elaborate. But she was clear about what she doesn't expect from this type of technology. "I certainly personally don't believe that a large portion of bookings are going to be an end-to-end conversational experience," she said. ... - Expedia is joining Meta's Muse agent and will judge future AI agent partnerships case by case, on top of existing ties to Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Claude, and Alexa. - Gorin doubts most bookings will become end-to-end chat transactions, and Expedia scrapped its single all-purpose agent for narrower point agents that each handle one part of planning. - AI tools have not lifted bookings yet, but they deliver more than 60% more data on traveler intent, higher engagement, and lower cancellations among those who book after using them. ... Expedia CEO Ariane Gorin used the Skift Global Forum stage to make a case for being everywhere AI agents live while doubting that any one agent will own the trip. Expedia confirmed this week that it is joining Muse, Meta's new AI agent, adding to integrations with Google's AI Mode, ChatGPT, Claude, and Amazon's Alexa. Gorin said she doesn't expect a large share of bookings to happen as one end-to-end conversational experience, since most trips involve several people and multiple rounds of consideration. Expedia abandoned its own single end-to-end agent in favor of specialized "point agents" that handle individual parts of shopping and planning, an approach its AI chief calls multi-agent architecture. The AI tools are not yet driving more bookings, but Gorin said they produce more engagement, more than 60% more information about what travelers want, and lower cancellation rates among people who book after using them. Asked why an AI platform should route through Expedia rather than go straight to hotels and airlines, Gorin pointed to fulfillment, customer service, payments, connectivity, selection, and bundling — the same argument Booking Holdings CEO Glenn Fogel made a day earlier. web.description: # Expedia is getting a direct line into Meta's agent. Your hotel can't apply for one. More than two million people downloaded Meta's AI agent in its first weeks. When they ask it for a hotel, Expedia will be the one it books inside the chat. Sep 25, 2026 by Markus Busch Meta's agent books travel now. On September 8, Meta launched Muse, an AI agent that runs errands instead of explaining them, from sending an email to buying a plane ticket. US travelers reach it in its own app or on WhatsApp, it's free to start, and by September 23 it had been downloaded more than two million times, CNN reported. On September 22, Expedia said it's joining, which means the agent will be able to book Expedia's hotels. No hotel company has been named alongside it. ... Expedia moves inside the chat. The deal puts Expedia on the short list. The guest will give the agent her dates, her city and what she's looking for, choose a hotel and pay without leaving the chat, PhocusWire reports. Expedia takes the payment, and what reaches your front desk is an Expedia reservation. Nobody is taking applications. Meta publishes no way for a hotel to ask for the same hookup, since Meta picked and built the list itself. There is a side door, though. A guest can connect the agent to a booking system on her own, as long as that system lets outside software make bookings on it. At your hotel, she would have to know you offer it, find it and type in a login, while the guest booking through Expedia won't have to know anything. The catch. Expedia's hotels aren't bookable in Muse yet, and no date has been given. Expedia hasn't explained how the hookup will work, and nobody has tested in public what the agent does when the same room is listed on Expedia and on your own site. ... Two weeks ago, Meta's agent read Expedia's website the same way it read yours, and now Expedia has signed up to be booked in the chat.

web.description: Date: September 24, 2026 08:09 Expedia has just sent two fairly clear signals about the direction travel distribution is taking. A user will be able to describe their needs in natural language, for example, searching for a hotel in Seattle from November 13th to 16th near the city center, and then receive a selection from Expedia's inventory. ... The traveler will be able to check prices, availability, room features and cancellation policies, compare several establishments and then proceed to payment without leaving Muse. For now, Muse integration is only announced in the United States. No French availability has been announced. ...
